title: Global quantum geometric Langlands at irrational level
main_claim: For G connected simple over C, a smooth projective curve X and every c in C minus Q, there is an equivalence D_c(Bun_G(X)) ≃ D_{-1/(rc)}(Bun_{G^vee}(X)) of twisted D-module categories, where D_c = D(L_G^{(c-h^vee)/(2h^vee)}) and r is the lacing number. The equivalence is characterized by a localization–Whittaker compatibility and matches central characters, components and central-torsor actions.

issues.location: Sec. 6, Lemma planch:satake-degree and Prop. planch:weight-estimate (06-plancherel.tex)
issues.description: I could not find a failing step here, but this is the most load-bearing new estimate and it only works if all its inputs hold. The uniform upper degree E is taken from the spectral side through GLC (Xi(V) for compact coherent C, Psi(C) bounded, and finite QCA cohomological dimension of LS). The finiteness of the contributing (c', l) pairs then depends on that bound being independent of the labels and the number of points, and on the link-degree count c'-2n. I checked the degree arithmetic: E + c' - 2n + 2n' = E - c'. The identification of the Fourier-specialized U'_0 with Hom(S Pvac_!, F_W) rests on Lin's vacuum comparison and the transpose argument, and I did not re-verify those.
issues.evidence: 'Configuration integration lowers this degree by the collision codimension, and the simplicial shifts lower it further. Only finitely many collision codimensions and simplicial degrees can therefore contribute to any fixed stalk degree'

issues.description: This is a new deformation argument and it is subtle; I checked it and it holds up. The weights of H^d(C_{i,n}) are bounded by C through the triangle C_{i,n-1}(1) -> C_{i,n} -> C_{i,1}. Generators that are homogeneous for Deligne's splitting are killed by strictness. The map M_i -> M_{i'} being zero gives a zero map over C((h)), hence generic rank zero, and Lemma deform:rank then gives rank zero at every q that is not a root of unity. The argument depends on Deligne-splitting lifts in the stabilized-image inverse system, which are only sketched.
issues.evidence: 'Deligne's functorial complex splitting ... permits a finite set of generators of this image to be chosen homogeneous for the weight splitting and lifted to weight-homogeneous elements of the inverse system.'

coverage: Read the introduction and the whole of Sec. 5 (deformation lemmas: Fourier comparison, rank test for q not a root of unity, logarithm colimit test, finite stages, Vinberg comparison), Sec. 6 (finite Whittaker test, separation lemma, vacuum weight bound, spectral degree bound, configuration estimate, Plancherel identity), Sec. 13 (localization, factorization lemma, construction of Phi with left and right inverses, sectors, central torsors), Sec. 2 (inertia vanishing and Harder–Narasimhan cutoff), and Sec. 9 up to Prop. local:one-slot (heart and realization, insertion, point gap). I checked by hand: the exponent bookkeeping s=(c+h^vee)/(2h^vee) = (c-h^vee)/(2h^vee)+1 and -s' = (-1/(rc)-check h^vee)/(2 check h^vee); the type-checking and composition of Psi_left Phi and Phi Psi_right; the relative-determinant character nu = sum over positive roots of 2ht(alpha)alpha = Kil(rho,-); the Riemann–Roch weight Q(z,u) and positivity through the inverse Cartan matrix; simplicity of Weyl modules at irrational level; and H^1 = H^2 = 0 for de Rham cohomology of semisimple G. Not read in detail: Secs. 3-4, 7-8, 10-12 (pseudo-identity, Whittaker models, loop categories, W-algebras, localization period comparison, unipotent and Ran periods). Cited external inputs (GLC I-V, Lin, Faergeman–Raskin, Arakawa–Frenkel, CDR) were not re-verified.
